issue_context.title: $fetch is not defined
issue_context.body: ### Environment ------------------------------ - Operating System: Darwin - Node Version: v16.20.0 - Nuxt Version: 3.8.0 - CLI Version: 3.9.1 - Nitro Version: 2.7.0 - Package Manager: yarn@1.22.19 - Builder: - - User Config: devServer, telemetry, imports, srcDir, app, runtimeConfig, css, vite, modules, vant, hooks, nitro, build - Runtime Modules: @qzd-h5-ui/nuxt@1.0.3, @vueuse/nuxt@10.5.0, @pinia/nuxt@0.4.11, @pinia-plugin-persistedstate/nuxt@1.1.2, nuxt-windicss@2.6.1 - Build Modules: - ------------------------------ ### Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-zr9tkf-upvvdt?file=utils%2Ffetch.ts ### Describe the bug The browser throws an error "$fetch is not defined". I need to call an API when initializing on the client side. I wrapped $fetch and exported a fetch function, calling the API request method in plugins/1.init.client.ts. ### Additional context ### Logs ```shell-script fetch.ts:1 Uncaught ReferenceError: $fetch is not defined at fetch.ts:1:14 ```
comments: _Start a new pull request in [StackBlitz Codeflow](https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/23848?repros=github-zr9tkf-upvvdt)._ - [**github-zr9tkf-upvvdt** (Open reproduction)](https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-zr9tkf-upvvdt?issueRepo=nuxt/nuxt&issueNumber=23848)

`$fetch` is actually never auto-imported, but rather, it's a global assignment: https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/755cf2053489e7d324abd4d43a73497d874e7754/packages/nuxt/src/app/entry.ts#L21-L26

While the case here is that the module has been imported in `entry.ts` before the `globalThis.$fetch = ` assignment.

A few solutions:

- Register it in auto-import entry - we would need a virtual file hosting that instance as `import { $fetch } from 'ofetch'` is not an equalivent because of the lack of baseUrl.
- Create a virtual file and run it beforehand, similar to `#build/paths.mjs`
- Ask user to explicitly import `$fetch` when using `$fetch.create` from top-level.
Interim solutions: Manually import $fetch

I would be open for an auto-import of `$fetch` ...

But I believe @pi0 has some reasons against it; see https://github.com/unjs/nitro/pull/742 and https://github.com/Baroshem/nuxt-security/issues/202#issuecomment-1708011762. Perhaps he could explain a bit more about why this is an issue.

For clarification, I'm not against this (factory) pattern but belive the root cause could be fixed differently than proposed PR.

Also following https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/14736, we can start with creating a stable `defineFetch` utility that lazily calls `$fetch` to avoid this ordering issue for when creating custom instance.
If you are up for it then I think we should revisit it. I think it might be worth it to avoid reliance on global variables, and to provide rollup with the right information about dependencies.

## Regarding Server/Nitro support of `$fetch`

As explained before, `fetch` and `$fetch` are initialized by the nitro app entry which is expected to be evaluated first. They are not like any other utility.

Using the auto import feature which is essentially a rollup transform plugin itself only works around this issue for bundled code that passes through rollup and can create future limitations (like assuming initialization is top level) and regressions if we go this path. Also manually importing `{ $fetch } from 'ofetch'` is not a solution or workaround unless we simply want a generic fetch. The `$fetch` instance injected by nitro app entry, is bound to the localFetch.

Nevertheless, I really like to fix this issue and unblock the supporting fetch factory pattern for Nuxt. 

Currently looking for a minimal reproduction ([this](https://stackblitz.com/edit/unjs-nitro-epop52?file=utils%2Findex.ts,routes%2Findex.ts,routes%2Ftest.ts&title=Nitro%20Starter) with nitro alone works for example) before attempting to fix it upstream.

## Regarding Client/Vite `$fetch`

Only about client-side fix, yes, using auto imports can possibly fix the issues as we are use everything is bundled and also have not the nitro app entry ordering concerns. (although, in the future if we want to integrate `$fetch` with nuxt custom caching or logging infra, it will be different from default `$fetch` export of `ofetch`...)

But if we go with auto import path, it means `$fetch` support would be inconsistent across different places.

## Conclusion

> @antfu Create a virtual file and run it beforehand, similar to #build/paths.mjs

I think this is closest possible solution to what i am thinking for nitro (once have exact reproduction) and also technically same idea of making sure rollup/vite know the correct dependency ordering so i would say worth to try this way 👍🏼

> Create a virtual file and run it beforehand, similar to #build/paths.mjs

Yes, this is what I was suggesting, assuming this virtual file supplies the auto-import of `$fetch`. 👌
Sounds good. In the future, I think `createFetch` (which can be auto-imported) would be better than `$fetch.create` indeed.
